preamble: The Middle Chinese palatal nasal initial (日母, Baxter ny-, Pulleyblank [ȵ], i.e. [ɲ]) did not merge with another initial in the north: it became a new voiced retroflex initial, written r- in pinyin and pronounced [ʐ] in free variation with [ɻ] in Standard Mandarin. The change is regular across the 日 class (日, 人, 熱, 肉, 然, 讓, 如), except before the rhymes that gave the syllable er (二, 兒, 耳, 而). Southern varieties give different outcomes, such as Cantonese [j], so the shift is confined to Mandarin.

examples.note: Wiktionary transcribes the initial as [ɻ]; Wikipedia's Standard Chinese phonology gives the phoneme as /ʐ/ with [ɻ] as a free variant.

sources: Pulleyblank, E. G. (1984). Middle Chinese: A Study in Historical Phonology. UBC Press. https://doi.org/10.59962/9780774854580
